title: Stability playbook, operator scripts, and status templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook bundles reproducible steps for stabilizing SLO regressions and degraded customer experiences, plus operator command snippets and copy-ready customer/status templates. The intent is low-friction action for oncall engineers, consistent external messaging, and a tight post-incident handoff to owners for corrective work.

Scope and services covered:
- Applies to hosted inference and Dedicated where Redwood controls routing: inference-gateway, traffic-router, runtime-pool, kv-cache-service, model-catalog, telemetry-proxy.
- Incident profiles: increased p99 latency, elevated 5xx rates, sudden throughput collapse, model-quality regressions detected by production evals.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Primary responder: service owner oncall (first responder). Executes fast containment and documents initial evidence.
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned for Sev2/Sev1. Orchestrates cross-team effort and updates stakeholders.
- Communications lead: crafts customer-facing notices and coordinates with CS.
- Engineering lead: drives root-cause diagnostics and fixes.

Severity thresholds (examples):
- Sev3 (degraded): p99 > baseline + 75ms for 10m OR 5xx > 0.5% for a production cluster.
- Sev2 (impacting): p99 > baseline + 250ms OR sustained 5xx > 2% OR RPS drop > 40% for >5m.
- Sev1 (outage): API unavailable for >=10% customers OR 5xx > 10% OR regional service loss.

Detect and observe (dashboards & queries):
- Key dashboards: SLO overview (p50/p95/p99), Error budget burn rate, KV cache hit/miss heatmap, Routing correctness map.
- Representative PromQL (p99 latency):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-gateway"}[1m])) by (le))
- Error rate (5xx):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-gateway",status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-gateway"}[1m]))

First-10-minute triage ladder (practical steps):
1) Verify alert signal across regions and scrape raw metrics to rule out alerting noise.
2) Check for recent deploys or config changes (traffic-router, inference-gateway, runtime-pool) in last 30m.
3) Inspect kv-cache metrics (evictions, load factor) and runtime CPU steal.
4) Identify if traffic concentration from a single tenant is present; if so proceed to tenant-scoped mitigation.

Containment runbooks (actionable):
A) High p99 latency (runtime or gateway)
- Trigger: p99 > baseline + 250ms for 5m.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Annotate incident ticket with snapshot of p50/p95/p99 and top-5 routes.
  2. Temporarily reduce batching window (batching-config.max_batch_ms from 50 -> 15).
  3. Scale runtime-pool up by 2x or add read replicas where possible.
  4. Flip routing fallback to lower-latency model variant for high-priority routes.
  5. If no improvement in 4m, shift 30-50% traffic to dedicated capacity or alternative region.

B) Cache thrash / evictions storm
- Trigger: eviction_rate > 1000/min or hit_rate < 25%.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Disable experimental prefetchers and non-critical cache writers.
  2. Increase per-node cache allocation by +20% for affected pools (ops change).
  3. If memory pressure persists, recycle one node at a time and observe recovery.
  4. If still unstable, remove affected pool from routing and route to fallback manifest.

C) Throughput collapse (RPS drop)
- Trigger: region RPS drops below 60% baseline for >3m.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Verify external dependency health (model-catalog, telemetry-proxy, data-plane storage).
  2. If telemetry sinks are slowing, temporarily disable non-essential telemetry.
  3. If model catalog is slow, switch to pinned manifest known-good (use admin API).
  4. Enable queued-burst-mode or tenant-level queueing to smooth bursts.

D) Model quality regression
- Trigger: production eval failure rate >5% AND user-reported quality issues.
- Immediate actions:
  1. Pause auto-rollout and pin traffic to last known-good model revision.
  2. Run fast evals against candidate model in isolated staging and compare token diffs.
  3. If rollback is necessary, perform rollback and notify CS with resolution ETA.

Tenant-scoped mitigations (noisy tenant handling):
- Use tenant-throttle and tenant-block endpoints. Standard slab: 10 QPS sustained, burst to 50 QPS for 30s.
- For repeat offenders, initiate billing review and escalate to CS/legal.

Operator quick commands (cheat sheet):
- Restart gateway: kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-gateway -n prod
- Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-gateway --to-revision=<n> -n prod
- Set fallback policy: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/v1/routing/set?policy=fast-variant
- PromQL snapshot CLI: promql -q 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-gateway"}[10m])) by (le))'

Customer communication templates (copy-ready):
- Initial (short):
  Subject: Investigating degraded inference performance in <region>
  Body: We are investigating higher-than-normal latency affecting Redwood's inference API in <region>. Our team is actively triaging. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. No action required from your side at this time.

- Follow-up (detailed operational):
  Subject: Update: mitigation in progress for inference degradation in <region>
  Body: Our investigation identified elevated cache evictions impacting p99 latency in <region>. Mitigations applied: scaled runtime pool, reduced batching window, and enabled a fallback model variant. Observed improvement: p99 decreased from X ms to Y ms. Next update in 60 minutes or upon significant change. For critical issues, contact support@redwood.com.

- Resolution notice (closing):
  Subject: Resolved: inference performance issue in <region>
  Body: The issue in <region> has been resolved. Root cause: excessive mem-pressure from a prefetcher overflowed KV cache entries and propagated latency to runtime. Fixes: prefetcher disabled, cache limits adjusted, pinned model manifest. We will publish a postmortem within 3 business days.

Status page messaging (public-friendly):
- Headline: Investigating increased latency for inference endpoints in <region>
- Body: We are investigating reports of increased response times that may affect some requests. Our oncall team is actively working on a mitigation. We will post updates here. Mapping: Sev1=Major outage, Sev2=Partial degradation, Sev3=Minor degradation.

Oncall rotation and wellbeing rules:
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary + 2-week secondary shadow.
- Maximum consecutive weeks: 3. HR/manager notified if exceeded.
- Swap policy: swaps allowed up to 48 hours before shift; must be recorded in the oncall calendar and #oncall Slack channel.
- Fatigue mitigation: auto-enroll engineers with >2 high-incident weeks in 30 days into a recovery week.

Quarterly game day scenarios (objectives embedded):
1) Cache storm: simulate eviction spike; objective: stabilize p99 within 20 minutes and validate customer messaging cadence.
2) Model regression drill: stage degraded model to validate fast rollback and eval pipeline; objective: complete rollback and publish customer-safe notice within 15 minutes.
3) Region failover: simulate region loss and exercise traffic-router fallbacks; objective: maintain >=90% baseline RPS within 10 minutes.

Post-incident checklist (IC completes within 24h):
- Confirm timeline and attach metric snapshots (start/peak/resolve).
- Document all commands and runbook steps executed.
- Record any privileged operations and link audit events.
- Assign postmortem author and create action items with owners/due dates.
- Notify CS/Finance/Legal if credits or regulatory reporting required.

Postmortem publishable structure (template):
1) Executive summary and impact window.
2) Minute-level timeline with key metric snapshots.
3) Root cause analysis and causal chain.
4) Short-term mitigations and long-term corrective actions.
5) Detection/alerting improvements and dashboards to add.
6) Action items with owners and due dates.
7) Lessons learned and product/process changes.

Escalation rules for Security/Legal/Finance:
- Suspected data exfiltration: IC pages Security within 15 minutes.
- Contractual SLO credit event: notify Finance and CS within 1 business day.

Runbook maintenance and governance:
- Each runbook requires a named owner and a quarterly review date. Owners must validate commands, dashboard links, and run at least one scenario annually.

Appendix 94 Evidence collection and useful snippets:
- Collect gateway logs for 15m: kubectl logs deploy/inference-gateway -n prod --since=15m --tail=500
- Fetch heap profile: curl http://<node-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap.prof
- Export Prometheus CSV snapshots and attach to incident ticket.

Contacts and notification endpoints (internal references):
- Oncall calendar: see internal oncall calendar URL
- SRE lead: sre-lead pager and Slack handle available in internal directory
- CS escalation: cs-ops@redwood.com

Change log (top-level edits):
- 2025-11-18: created stability playbook and templates (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-01-12: tightened cache runbook and added tenant throttle defaults (Miguel Hernandez).
- 2026-02-15: updated game day objectives and post-incident checklist (Claire Thompson).

Related resources:
- Grafana SLO dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/inference/slo-overview
- Runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-library
- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

If you are the oncall and encounter an uncovered condition, escalate to the SRE lead and open a sprint ticket to capture the missing runbook step.
